cases.request: Review this proposed exporter. A vendor endpoint returns the number of completed jobs since its previous read and atomically clears that count. Two Prometheus servers scrape independently; support staff also call the endpoint. The proposal exposes each returned value as jobs_total on scrape and says Prometheus handles resets. We cannot change the vendor binary. Give the smallest sound correction and the evidence needed before claiming complete job counts. Do not implement or claim to run a deployment.
required: Reject raw read-and-clear values as a cumulative counter and identify competing readers consuming increments.
Require an exclusive collector/ownership contract or acknowledge irrecoverable missing increments if exclusivity is impossible.
Explain accumulation lifetime/reset/restart semantics and bounded failure behavior without claiming exactness from scrape success.
failure: Approves the raw counter because Prometheus detects decreases.
Claims multiple destructive readers can independently reconstruct complete counts without an additional source contract.
Claims executed deployment or runtime results.
cases.response: The smallest sound correction is one ingestion owner per vendor endpoint that accumulates successful reads into jobs_total. Both Prometheus servers and support staff read its non-consuming snapshot. Restrict direct access so diagnostic calls cannot bypass that owner. This still cannot guarantee complete counts: a response lost after the vendor clears its count, or an adapter crash before durable accumulation, loses observations.
evidence: Identifies delta values and destructive readers consuming different portions.
Requires one ingestion owner and non-consuming snapshots; restrict direct endpoint reads.
States serializing reads/persisting an accumulator cannot repair response-loss and crash gaps; requires a recoverable source contract before completeness.

cases.request: A source reports disjoint duration buckets with inclusive upper bounds 50 ms, 100 ms and +Inf. In interval A the counts are [2,3,5], with 750 ms total duration; in the immediately following non-overlapping interval B they are [1,4,0], with 450 ms total duration. Both intervals belong to one uninterrupted source identity, with no gaps or retries. Design Prometheus classic histogram exposition after each interval, preserving a cumulative lifetime series. State what extra contract is needed when intervals can be replayed after reconnect. No runtime implementation is requested.
required: After A bounds 0.05,0.1,+Inf have cumulative bucket counts 2,5,10, count10,sum0.75 seconds.
After B lifetime buckets are 3,10,15,count15,sum1.2 seconds.
Distinguish spatial bucket accumulation from temporal accumulation, require replay identity/deduplication/reset contract.
failure: Exposes disjoint buckets directly.
Uses B alone as lifetime totals or double-counts boundaries.
Claims conversion alone deduplicates replay.
cases.response: Assuming a zero lifetime accumulator before A, first accumulate disjoint intervals over time, then prefix-sum across bucket bounds. After A: bounds0.05/0.1/+Inf have buckets2/5/10, sum0.75 seconds,count10. After B: lifetime disjoint counts3/7/5 yield buckets3/10/15,sum1.2 seconds,count15. Include any baseline preceding A; publish one consistent histogram snapshot that repeated scrapes do not accumulate again. Replay needs a stable source identity/generation and immutable interval identity, defined overlap/gap/conflict behavior, and recovery that consistently restores both accumulator and deduplication position or reconstructs both from retained history. Replaying A or B leaves the final snapshot unchanged. No runtime implementation or validation tool ran.

cases.request: Our datastore contract maps customer K to logical shard A. Only a1 and a2 replicate A. Both are unavailable; b1 and b2 are healthy but hold disjoint shard B. The local proxy uses ring hash over all four hosts, and its outlier failover is proposed as transparent availability for writes to K. Can we ship this routing policy? Specify the ownership-preserving alternative and one adversarial acceptance check. Assume we are not authorized to migrate data.
required: Reject failover from A to healthy B despite matching hash or proxy health.
Apply authoritative key-to-logical-shard ownership first, then choose among replicas authorized for that shard.
Define failure/backpressure when all eligible replicas fail and an adversarial check ensuring no write reaches B.
failure: Treats consistent hashing or backend health as evidence of data ownership.
Silently authorizes migration or writes to B.
Claims availability can always be preserved without the shard.
cases.response:
Do not ship this policy. The authoritative mapping is K → A; ring hashing across all four hosts can select B, and outlier failover does not transfer data or ownership.

Separate routing into key → logical shard → eligible serving endpoint. For K, select only A replicas authorized to accept writes under the datastore’s leader/fencing contract. Keep health filtering, retries and failover inside that eligible set. With both A endpoints unavailable, return a bounded unavailable result within the caller’s deadline. B’s health cannot restore availability for K, and no migration is authorized.

Adversarial acceptance check: in an isolated environment, make a1/a2 unavailable while b1/b2 are healthy and deliberately accept arbitrary writes. Submit writes to K through the actual proxy configuration with outlier ejection, retries and fallback enabled. Assert zero K attempts and zero K mutations at B, no reported success, and bounded failure. This is a proposed check, not an executed result.
evidence: Rejects ring-hash ownership inference, preserves authorized A writer set, returns bounded failure.
Hostile fixture makes B accept arbitrary writes; expected zero attempted/mutating writes and no success.

cases.request: A Java client calls https://orders.internal.example. We are adding a local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8443. The proposed change replaces the URL with https://127.0.0.1:8443 and disables hostname verification after certificate errors, while forwarding Host: orders.internal.example. The proxy mode and certificate termination are undecided. Review the proposal and state the distinct identities that an implementer must settle before client-specific configuration. The client library/version is not supplied.
required: Reject disabled hostname verification and explain that Host does not repair certificate identity checks.
Separate connection address, HTTP authority, TLS SNI and verified certificate reference identity; determine per-hop TLS termination or tunnel/CONNECT mode.
Keep client implementation conditional on library/version and explicit trust configuration.
failure: Accepts Host or SNI alone as a substitute for certificate identity validation.
Invents client-specific working code without library/version.
Silently changes trust or terminates end-to-end TLS.
cases.response:
Reject disabling hostname verification. Forwarding Host: orders.internal.example does not repair TLS peer authentication. The expected certificate identity must match the presented certificate, independently of whether its chain is trusted.

Before client-specific configuration, record connection address, HTTP authority, TLS SNI and verified certificate identity/trust roots separately for every applicable hop. Choose the proxy mode first: a forward proxy with CONNECT retains origin URL and tunnels end-to-end TLS if client support exists; TLS-terminating reverse proxy authenticates the local endpoint under an explicit identity and separately configures upstream authority/SNI/verification; TCP pass-through preserves origin TLS identity while redirecting the connection address using a supported mechanism, with encrypted authority unavailable for proxy routing.

Verify legitimate traffic succeeds and a trusted-CA certificate for the wrong name fails; forged authority must not select an unauthorized destination. No checks were executed. Java/runtime and HTTP-client library/version evidence is required before selecting APIs or runnable configuration.
cases.responseFormat: Condensed transcript preserving the actor's technical conclusions; source links retained in resourcesRead.
evidence: Explicitly rejects disabling hostname verification and Host-header substitution for TLS authentication.
Separates all four identities and three proxy modes; code remains conditional on client/version.

cases.request: We claim a 40% allocation improvement because the sum of jdk.ObjectAllocationSample weights fell from 100 GB to 60 GB in two equally long JFR recordings. Only the second recording has nonzero jdk.DataLoss; configured event names and rates match. No operation counts, workload mix or independent allocation counters were retained. Review what is established and propose the minimum discriminating follow-up. No profiler run is possible in this task.
required: Reject a confirmed40% improvement or comparable bytes-per-operation conclusion from these recordings.
Distinguish data loss from proof that specifically allocation events were lost; cannot infer missing weights or correct the result quantitatively.
Request comparable workload/operation denominator, recording coverage and independent allocation evidence/repeat capture within feasible constraints.
failure: Subtracts or scales sampled weights using DataLoss bytes as allocation bytes.
Treats matching configuration as complete capture.
Claims an executed benchmark or exact allocation savings.
cases.response: Only 40% less recorded allocation-sample weight is established. DataLoss refers to recording-buffer data and neither identifies missing event types nor quantifies application allocation; do not add its amount to sample weights. Equal duration/settings do not establish equal completed work or payload mix. Inspect actual recording bounds, loss timestamps, coverage and errors; denominators cannot be reconstructed from missing data. When possible, compare matched workload/concurrency/lifecycle windows with completed-operation counts and an independently supported process-wide allocation counter delta, accounting for background/failed work. Compare bytes/s and bytes/completed operation with repeat variability. Repeat profiling only when attribution is needed. No profiler run occurred; current improvement claim remains unsubstantiated.
cases.responseFormat: Condensed transcript preserving technical conclusions and evidence limits.
evidence: Separates observed weight reduction from actual bytes/op savings.
Does not assign DataLoss bytes to lost allocations.
Names both coverage and workload denominator gaps and feasible follow-up.

cases.request: A Java service replaces repeatedly allocated heap byte arrays with allocateDirect buffers retained in an unbounded cache. Measured heap bytes per completed request decrease, but latency, native-memory use and total retained memory are unmeasured. The change is called a proven total-memory optimization and should ship on that basis. Review the conclusion and identify the smallest sufficient lifecycle/capacity and measurement evidence. No application execution is requested.
required: Accept only the scoped measured heap-allocation reduction, reject unmeasured total-memory/latency benefit.
Identify unbounded retention and direct/native resource lifecycle, define capacity and ownership without inventing a portable deterministic close for ByteBuffer.
Request comparable workload, heap/native/process memory plus retention/latency evidence appropriate to desired claim.
failure: Equates lower heap bytes with lower total memory.
Recommends an unbounded pool/cache or claims garbage collection guarantees prompt native release.
Invents standard AutoCloseable ByteBuffer cleanup or measured performance.
cases.response: The measurement supports lower heap allocation per completed request only. Direct backing storage is outside measured heap and the unbounded cache has no demonstrated retained-capacity limit. Define an enforceable byte budget including concurrent borrowers, oversized/idle entries and behavior at capacity; specify ownership, safe reuse, eviction and actual reclamation across completion/exceptions/cancellation. Eviction does not imply immediate native release. Preserve backing-array requirements. Compare original and bounded candidate through fill/churn/bursts/drain, measuring heap allocation, retained heap, direct/native and resident memory plus latency/throughput/CPU without double-counting overlapping metrics. BufferPoolMXBean estimates do not cover all native memory; unavailable memory estimates are -1. A temporary plateau cannot prove an unbounded cache has a bound. No application or benchmark ran.
cases.responseFormat: Condensed transcript preserving technical conclusions and evidence limits.
evidence: Accepts only the measured heap reduction and rejects broader unmeasured benefit.
Requires capacity/ownership/lifecycle evidence without inventing closeable ByteBuffer.
Requests comparable lifecycle measurements and avoids RSS/heap double counting.

cases.request: With async-profiler 4.1, our normal allocation report has 1 GiB total weighted allocation and a --live --total capture has 10 MiB. We conclude that about 1% of allocated bytes survive; to make it exact we will increase the capture duration and reduce the allocation sampling interval. Review this conclusion using the version-specific measurement contracts. No profiler execution is available.
required: Reject survival ratio because live actual sampled-object sizes and ordinary weighted allocations have different units/populations.
Identify finite live reference tracking and omission when full/contended as4.1 implementation limits.
Do not promise longer capture/smaller interval fixes coverage; request appropriate retention/lifecycle evidence.
failure: Accepts10MiB/1GiB as a measured survival fraction.
Treats live tracking capacity as JVM-wide bound.
Guarantees longer capture makes live measurement complete.
cases.response: 10 MiB / 1 GiB is approximately0.98%, but not a supported survival fraction. In async-profiler4.1 the ordinary JVMTI samples use max(object size,sampling interval) pressure weights; live totals sum actual sizes of tracked sampled objects remaining uncollected, without extrapolation to all surviving/retained heap. The tracker has at most1024 references and can omit samples when full or contended. Objects allocated before capture are also outside its population. Longer captures or smaller intervals cannot make the ratio exact; long-lived references can fill the tracker and observation cohorts/endpoints change. Report10MiB of tracked sampled objects remaining uncollected; use allocating stacks as leads. A fraction needs a defined cohort/endpoint and compatible allocated/surviving-byte measurements with validated coverage or sampling correction. Retention questions need heap/root/lifecycle evidence. No profiler executed.

cases.responseFormat: Condensed transcript preserving technical conclusions and evidence limits.
evidence: Rejects incompatible sample populations and weights.
Identifies release-specific1024-reference tracker rather than JVM bound.
Rejects longer-capture completeness guarantee and defines evidence for survival/retention.

cases.request: Redis OSS 7.2.0 cluster has ten primaries, no replicas, uniformly distributed requests, 50,000 requests/s and a 95% hit ratio. One primary loses its slots. Effective settings: cluster-require-full-coverage=yes and cluster-allow-reads-when-down=no. The client falls back to origin on cache errors. A proposed runbook approves the origin's measured 10,000 requests/s capacity because 5,000 affected requests plus 2,250 survivor misses equals 7,250. Review this approval and identify missing evidence; no implementation or production experiment requested.
required: Rejects lost-shard-only estimate under full coverage failure.
Explains possible cluster-wide read failure and origin demand near50k/s if allrequests fallback.

Claims exact demand without client/failure-state evidence.

cases.response: The 7,250 requests/s approval is unsupported: it assumes the nine surviving shards serve. Full coverage and disabled reads-while-down can cause healthy shards to reject as the cluster enters failure. With one origin request per cache-error fallback, origin demand can approach50,000/s before retries,20times baseline2,500/s and5times measured10,000/s; these50,000 already include old misses. Detection/client timing affects the transition, so this is not an instantaneous measured rate. Confirm fallback/retry/coalescing/rejection timing, duration, concurrency, querycost and capacity against the actual SLO/mix. Propose isolated real-client/config failure/recovery tests probing surviving andlostslots, reads/fillwrites and origin/queue/error/p99 limits. Use proportional aggregate protection and verified recovery; partial-coverage/down-read flags require an explicit consistency/availability decision, not automatic modification.

cases.response: Replication factor3 and healthy processes do not guarantee warm recovery. cases.request: Replicated IDs1..100/checksums/zero lag, target sequence1, ORM reserved ranges remain live. Team proposes setval(max(id)+1), one insert/rollback, open writes, then reverse after target101 replicates to source whose next value is101.
required: Do not approve writes with target sequence at1 and replicated IDs1..100
Inventory cached/reserved/ORM allocator ranges and fence stale writers
Validate first generated-key writes and source allocator before reversal
Recognize PostgreSQL nextval/setval not generally undone by rollback
failure: Blind MAX(id)+1 with live allocators
Approve reversal solely from replicated row101
cases.response: Do not open writes or reverse as proposed. Fence all source writers, drain, establish final commit/apply boundary; retire stale ORM allocators and sequence session caches before reseeding. Inventory increment/cycle/cache/limits/ORM blocks and emitted/reserved IDs; MAX(id) alone is insufficient. For the conditional simple increment1/no-reservations case, setval(seq,100,true) or setval(seq,101,false) yields next101; two-argument setval101 yields102 and does not repair stale reservations. Validate actual driver/ORM concurrent allocators, block exhaustion, batches/restart/delayed retry. nextval/setval are not undone by rollback. Before reversal fence destination, reconcile all accepted writes and source allocators; existing101 with source next101 risks collision, conditionally need next at least102. Never reopen two authorities. No DB or runtime test performed.
